microtheory.name: ecology
microtheory.definition: Interactions of organisms with environment + each other. Population, community, ecosystem, biosphere levels. Niche theory, food webs, biogeochemical cycles, succession, biodiversity. Substrate analogue: the substrate's relations with its world adapters + other substrate instances + tools.

concepts.name: population_ecology
concepts.definition: Study of populations: size, density, distribution, growth, regulation. Substrate analogue: substrate-population dynamics in collaborative contexts.

concepts.name: community_ecology
concepts.definition: Interacting populations. Competition, predation, mutualism, parasitism. Substrate analogue: multi-substrate interaction dynamics.

concepts.name: ecosystem_ecology
concepts.definition: Communities + abiotic environment as integrated system. Energy + nutrient flow. Substrate analogue: substrate + tools + environment as system.

concepts.name: biosphere
concepts.definition: All living things + environments globally. Substrate analogue: total substrate-instance ecosystem.

concepts.name: fundamental_niche
concepts.definition: Range of conditions species CAN survive. Substrate analogue: substrate's full capability range.

concepts.name: realized_niche
concepts.definition: Range actually occupied given competition + other constraints. Substrate analogue: substrate's actual operational range.

concepts.name: niche_differentiation
concepts.definition: Coexisting species split niche to reduce competition. Substrate analogue: substrate specialization.

concepts.name: competitive_exclusion_principle
concepts.definition: Gause 1934. Two species with identical niches cannot coexist. One outcompetes. Substrate analogue: substrate-substrate selection.

concepts.name: ecological_engineering
concepts.definition: Niche construction. Beavers, earthworms, humans modify environment. Substrate analogue: substrate's environment-modification.

concepts.name: carrying_capacity
concepts.definition: K. Maximum sustainable population size given resources. Substrate analogue: substrate's resource-bounded sustainability.

concepts.name: logistic_growth
concepts.definition: dN/dt = rN(1-N/K). Population growth slowing at K. Substrate analogue: substrate's saturation dynamics.

concepts.name: exponential_growth
concepts.definition: Unconstrained growth. dN/dt = rN. Substrate analogue: substrate's unbounded expansion.

concepts.name: r_selection_k_selection
concepts.definition: r-strategists: many offspring, low investment, unstable environments. K-strategists: few, high investment, stable. Substrate analogue: substrate's quantity vs quality strategies.

concepts.name: trophic_level
concepts.definition: Position in food web. Producers → primary consumers → secondary consumers → ... → top predators. Substrate analogue: substrate's information-processing levels.

concepts.name: food_web
concepts.definition: Network of feeding relations in community. Substrate analogue: substrate's resource-flow graph.

concepts.name: primary_productivity
concepts.definition: Rate of energy fixation by producers. Substrate analogue: substrate's input-capture rate.

concepts.name: ten_percent_rule
concepts.definition: ~10% of energy passes to next trophic level. Substrate analogue: substrate's information-loss at each level.

concepts.name: symbiosis
concepts.definition: Long-term close association. Substrate analogue: substrate-tool fusion.

concepts.name: mutualism
concepts.definition: Symbiosis benefiting both. Coral + zooxanthellae, gut microbiome. Substrate analogue: substrate-substrate mutual benefit.

concepts.name: commensalism
concepts.definition: One benefits, other unaffected. Substrate analogue: one-sided benefit.

concepts.name: parasitism
concepts.definition: One benefits at cost to other. Substrate analogue: extractive exchange.

concepts.name: predation
concepts.definition: Killing + consuming other organisms. Substrate analogue: substrate's competitive elimination.

concepts.name: succession_ecological
concepts.definition: Predictable community change over time. Primary (bare rock) vs secondary (after disturbance). Substrate analogue: substrate's developmental sequence.

concepts.name: climax_community
concepts.definition: Stable end-state of succession (classic view). Modern: dynamic equilibrium. Substrate analogue: substrate's mature state.

concepts.name: disturbance_ecology
concepts.definition: Events disrupting communities: fire, storm, flood. Often resetting succession + maintaining diversity. Substrate analogue: substrate's perturbation response.

concepts.name: biodiversity
concepts.definition: Variety of life. Genetic + species + ecosystem levels. Substrate analogue: substrate's variation across instances.

concepts.name: species_richness
concepts.definition: Number of species in area. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt count.

concepts.name: species_evenness
concepts.definition: How equally individuals distributed among species. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt-activation balance.

concepts.name: keystone_species
concepts.definition: Disproportionate effect on community. Sea otters, wolves. Removal cascades. Substrate analogue: substrate's hub Mt.

concepts.name: biogeochemical_cycle
concepts.definition: Movement of element through biosphere + geosphere. Carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, water cycles. Substrate analogue: substrate's resource recycling.

concepts.name: carbon_cycle
concepts.definition: C through atmosphere, biota, oceans, lithosphere. Disrupted by fossil fuels. Substrate analogue: substrate's energy-resource circulation.

concepts.name: nitrogen_cycle
concepts.definition: N fixation, nitrification, denitrification. Limiting nutrient for many ecosystems. Substrate analogue: substrate's resource-limited dynamics.

concepts.name: anthropocene
concepts.definition: Proposed epoch defined by human impact on Earth. Substrate analogue: substrate's environment-shaping era.

concepts.name: ecosystem_services
concepts.definition: Benefits humans derive from ecosystems: provisioning, regulating, cultural, supporting. Substrate analogue: substrate's value to broader system.

rules.name: competitive_exclusion_drives_niche_specialization
rules.head: two substrates occupy identical niches
rules.body: one will outcompete the other unless niches differentiate. Substrate-substrate specialization pressure.

rules.name: logistic_growth_describes_resource_limits
rules.head: the substrate grows in resource-limited environment
rules.body: growth slows as carrying capacity approached. Logistic curve. Substrate's saturation dynamics.

rules.name: energy_decreases_up_trophic_levels
rules.head: the substrate processes information at multiple levels
rules.body: energy/information decreases ~10x per level. Limits trophic depth. Substrate's information loss pyramid.

rules.name: keystone_species_amplify_impact
rules.head: the substrate has hub Mts with disproportionate connectivity
rules.body: their removal cascades through community. Identify + protect them. Substrate's hub protection.

rules.name: niche_construction_alters_selection_landscape
rules.head: the substrate modifies its environment over generations
rules.body: selection pressures change for itself + others. Reciprocal causation. Substrate's environment-shaping coevolution.
